research_question: What are the evidence-based, teachable principles of design consistency via design systems — specifically design tokens (color/space/type/radius/elevation as named variables, not ad-hoc values), component-library usage (primitives over raw elements), one unified visual language, and design-to-build handoff fidelity — that let an AI designer agent PASS/FAIL a rendered UI on the design-tokens, component-usage, and design-handoff axes?

phases.name: Landscape
phases.objective: Survey the canonical principle authorities on consistency and design systems: NN/g consistency-and-standards heuristic, Jakob's Law, the W3C Design Tokens Community Group token taxonomy (global/alias/component tokens), Material 3 token tiers (reference/system/component), and the component-library / single-source-of-truth model.
sub_questions: What is the agreed definition and tier model of a design token (reference vs system/semantic vs component-specific)?
Why does consistency reduce cognitive load and error (Jakob's Law, internal vs external consistency, recognition over recall)?
phases.evidence_priorities: NN/g consistency article + 10 heuristics; W3C design-tokens-format spec; Material 3 tokens; Refactoring UI on defining systems (color shades, spacing scale, type scale); Laws of UX Jakob's Law.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when the token tier model, the consistency rationale, and the component-library SSOT model are each documented with a primary source.

phases.name: Mechanics
phases.objective: How consistency is operationalized in a modern Next.js/Tailwind/Radix/shadcn substrate: CSS custom properties as the token layer (--primary, --background, oklch), @theme exposure to utilities, CVA variant primitives, semantic vs raw color naming, the spacing/type scale, and a design→build handoff that preserves intent (named tokens, component contracts, prop typing).
sub_questions: How do semantic/aliased tokens (e.g. --primary, --destructive) decouple intent from raw value and enable theming/dark-mode?
What makes a component-library primitive (variant-driven Button) the right unit vs a raw <button>, and what is a faithful handoff (spec component → real ui/ primitive)?
phases.evidence_priorities: Refactoring UI color/spacing/type systems; W3C token spec alias tokens; shadcn/CVA variant patterns (as principle source, not a product rec); Material 3 component tokens; design-handoff fidelity writing.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when token-layering, semantic naming, primitive-variant, and handoff-fidelity mechanics each have a concrete teachable example.

phases.name: Failure Modes
phases.objective: What breaks consistency: hardcoded hex/raw values bypassing tokens, raw Tailwind theme color utilities (bg-blue-500) instead of semantic tokens, one-off raw <button>/<input> instead of the library primitive, untyped (any) props, token drift / forking the system, inconsistent terminology, mismatched dark-mode values, and handoff drift where the build silently diverges from the spec.
sub_questions: What are the most common, mechanically-detectable token/consistency violations and how do they read to the user (brand drift, inconsistent spacing, broken dark mode)?
How does a 'use the system, don't fork it' violation propagate cost across a codebase?
phases.evidence_priorities: Design-system governance post-mortems; token-drift / hardcoded-value anti-patterns; NN/g inconsistency cost; component-library adoption-failure writeups.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 5+ distinct, detectable consistency failure modes are documented with how each reads to the user.

phases.name: Contrarian
phases.objective: When does rigid consistency hurt? Tesler's Law / necessary complexity, when a one-off override is legitimate (allow-list discipline), 'consistency for its own sake' vs purposeful inconsistency (Von Restorff — the deliberately-different element), and the cost/overhead of a design system for small projects.
sub_questions: When is breaking consistency the right call, and how should an agent distinguish a legitimate exception (allow-listed, documented) from drift?
phases.evidence_priorities: Critiques of over-systematization; purposeful-deviation writing; allow-list / exception-governance patterns; Tesler's Law.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ substantive cases for legitimate inconsistency are documented with how to govern the exception.

openai_instructions: Map every consistency principle to a MECHANICALLY-DETECTABLE rule an automated reviewer could PASS/FAIL: e.g. 'no hex literal in className/style', 'no raw Tailwind theme color utility for theme colors', 'interactive element must be a library primitive', 'props must be typed (no any)', 'required design-system docs must exist', 'token resolves to var(--...) not ad-hoc'. Build a fault tree from 'inconsistent UI' down to the specific detectable code/computed-style signature. Prioritize the design-tokens, component-usage, and design-handoff review axes.
